title: A Friend Watched Lizzie Borden Burn a Dress. The Jury Still Acquitted Her.

narration: Days after the killings, a friend watched Lizzie Borden burn a dress.
A jury still acquitted her.
shots.visual_description: lb8 kitchen (warm grade); lb8_alice: stand -> hand_to_face -> hands_together; lb8_lizzie: stand -> present -> stand -> focused; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label 'DAYS AFTER THE KILLINGS', stamp 'ACQUITTED · 1893'.

sources.claim_text: Family friend Alice Russell testified at the 1893 trial that on the Sunday after the killings (7 Aug 1892) she saw Lizzie burn a dress in the kitchen stove.
On 20 June 1893 a jury in New Bedford acquitted Lizzie Borden of the murders.

narration: You've seen the Netflix show. Here's what the record says.
shots.visual_description: lb8 parlour (sepia grade); lb8_lizzie: hands_together -> stand; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'THE DRAMA', label 'THE RECORD'.

sources.claim_text: Netflix's Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story (a dramatisation) premiered on 17 Sept 2026 and topped Netflix's English TV chart. The episode is scripted from the historical record, not the drama.

narration: In August 1892, Andrew and Abby Borden were killed in their Fall River home.
shots.visual_description: lb8 house (sepia grade); lb8_neighbour: stand -> worried -> hand_to_face; lb8_officer: walk -> stand (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: label '4 AUGUST 1892'.

sources.claim_text: Andrew Borden and his second wife, Abby, were killed in their home in Fall River, Massachusetts, on 4 Aug 1892.

narration: Abby wasn't Lizzie's mother. She was her stepmother.
So that famous rhyme gets it wrong.
shots.visual_description: lb8 parlour (sepia grade); lb8_lizzie [house]: stand -> hands_together -> arms_crossed -> neutral; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'ANDREW BORDEN · FATHER / ABBY BORDEN · STEPMOTHER', funfact 'The famous playground rhyme / calls Abby Lizzie's ‘mother’. / She was her STEPMOTHER.'.

overlays.text: ANDREW BORDEN · FATHER / ABBY BORDEN · STEPMOTHER
The famous playground rhyme / calls Abby Lizzie's ‘mother’. / She was her STEPMOTHER.

sources.claim_text: Abby Borden was Andrew's second wife and Lizzie's stepmother, not her mother.
The anonymous playground rhyme calls Abby Lizzie's 'mother'; she was her stepmother. (The rhyme's other details are also inaccurate; they are not repeated in the episode.)

narration: A week later, police arrested Lizzie.
shots.visual_description: lb8 house (warm grade); lb8_lizzie: stand_tense -> hands_together (walks); lb8_officer: stand -> present -> hands_behind; lb8_officer: hands_behind (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'ARRESTED'.

sources.claim_text: Lizzie Borden was arrested on 11 Aug 1892, one week after the killings.

narration: In June 1893, she stood trial for murder in New Bedford.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (sepia grade); judge: sit; judge: sit_read -> gavel -> sit; judge: sit; lb8_juror: sit; lb8_juror [grey]: sit; lb8_juror [brown]: sit; lb8_juror: sit; lb8_lizzie [court]: sit -> worried; lb8_lawyer: hands_behind -> point -> present; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'NEW BEDFORD · JUNE 1893'.

sources.claim_text: Her murder trial opened in New Bedford, Massachusetts, on 5 June 1893.

narration: Newspapers across the country followed every day.
shots.visual_description: press hall (sepia grade); lb8_juror [grey]: walk -> read_newspaper (walks); lb8_juror [shirtsleeves]: read_newspaper -> shocked -> stand; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label 'COAST TO COAST'.

sources.claim_text: The trial was a national press sensation: newspapers from across the country covered it, carried nationwide by wire services.

narration: Then the court excluded her own inquest testimony,
and a clerk who said she tried to buy poison the day before.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (sepia grade); judge: sit_read -> gavel -> sit -> gavel -> sit; lb8_lawyer: present -> stand_tense -> point -> hands_behind; keyed camera moves; overlays: card 'LIZZIE'S OWN / INQUEST TESTIMONY', stamp 'EXCLUDED', card 'A CLERK SAID SHE TRIED / TO BUY PRUSSIC ACID / THE DAY BEFORE', stamp 'EXCLUDED'.

overlays.text: A CLERK SAID SHE TRIED / TO BUY PRUSSIC ACID / THE DAY BEFORE

sources.claim_text: The court excluded Lizzie's own inquest testimony from the trial.
A drugstore clerk (Eli Bence) said Lizzie tried to buy prussic acid, a poison, on 3 Aug 1892, the day before the killings; the court excluded this testimony from the trial.

narration: But her friend Alice Russell testified.
The Sunday after the killings, she saw Lizzie burning a dress in the stove.
shots.visual_description: lb8 kitchen (sepia grade); lb8_alice: stand -> hands_together -> realise -> hand_to_face; lb8_lizzie: stand -> present -> stand; keyed camera moves; overlays: label 'ALICE RUSSELL', label 'SUNDAY, 7 AUGUST 1892'.

sources.claim_text: Family friend Alice Russell testified at the 1893 trial that on the Sunday after the killings (7 Aug 1892) she saw Lizzie burn a dress in the kitchen stove.

narration: Lizzie said it was stained with paint.
Prosecutors said she was destroying evidence.
shots.visual_description: lb8 kitchen (warm grade); lb8_lizzie: stand -> hands_together -> worried; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'HER EXPLANATION: / STAINED WITH PAINT', card 'THE PROSECUTION: / DESTROYING EVIDENCE'.

sources.claim_text: According to Alice Russell's testimony, Lizzie said she was burning the dress because it was stained (covered) with paint.
Prosecutors argued the burning was the destruction of evidence. This was the prosecution's argument; the jury acquitted her.

narration: No weapon was ever conclusively tied to her.
After about ninety minutes, the jury said: not guilty.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (sepia grade); judge: sit -> gavel -> sit; lb8_juror: sit -> stand -> point; lb8_juror [grey]: sit; lb8_juror [brown]: sit; lb8_lizzie [court]: hands_together -> worried -> hand_to_face -> bowed; keyed camera moves; overlays: card 'MURDER WEAPON: / NEVER CONCLUSIVELY / TIED TO HER', label '20 JUNE 1893', stamp 'NOT GUILTY'.

overlays.text: MURDER WEAPON: / NEVER CONCLUSIVELY / TIED TO HER

sources.claim_text: No murder weapon was ever conclusively tied to Lizzie; the case against her was circumstantial.
The jury deliberated for about 90 minutes before returning its not-guilty verdict (HISTORY.com and Biography.com; one outlet gives 65 minutes, so the episode says 'about').
On 20 June 1893 a jury in New Bedford acquitted Lizzie Borden of the murders.

narration: She stayed in Fall River, in a grand house she named Maplecroft.
Many shunned her until her death in 1927.
shots.visual_description: lb8 house (dawn grade); lb8_lizzie [house]: walk -> sad -> bowed (walks); lb8_neighbour: stand -> hands_together; lb8_juror [brown]: stand -> hands_behind; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'MAPLECROFT', label 'FALL RIVER, 1893-1927'.

sources.claim_text: After the trial she stayed in Fall River and, with her sister Emma, bought a large house they named Maplecroft.
She was widely shunned in Fall River for the rest of her life and died there on 1 June 1927.

narration: And the house where it happened is now a bed and breakfast.
Yes, you can stay the night.
shots.visual_description: lb8 house (night grade); camera push/pull; overlays: label 'TODAY', funfact 'The Borden house is now a / museum + bed & breakfast. / Yes: guests stay overnight.'.

overlays.text: The Borden house is now a / museum + bed & breakfast. / Yes: guests stay overnight.

sources.claim_text: The Second Street house where the killings happened is now the Lizzie Borden House, a museum and bed and breakfast where guests can stay overnight.

narration: Officially unsolved. Would you have acquitted her?

sources.claim_text: Lizzie Borden was acquitted and no one else was ever tried: the killings remain officially unsolved.
On 20 June 1893 a jury in New Bedford acquitted Lizzie Borden of the murders.
Agatha Christie disappeared on 3 Dec 1926 and was found 11 days later at a hotel in Harrogate (next episode tease).
